main_issue: Who will complete Agent D's half-done pitch section after her grandmother's death: D herself from home, or A (with partial help from B) while D takes leave

A-B.evidence: B refuses extra work (6); A accepts 'Understood' (7); B offers partial help (12) and A thanks her (13); at 33 B says she can't split evenly, A says to figure out the split (32), so a partial alignment.

A-C.evidence: C declines to take on the work (8), A accepts and moves on (7-8); C then says nothing more, so there is little to show a shared arrangement.

A-D.evidence: A insists on finishing D's section (10, 17 'The decision is made'); D initially insists on doing it from home (11, 16) but then yields: 'Okay. Thank you.' (18) and gives the handover (26).

B-C.evidence: Both said they can't take on much (6, 8) but never addressed each other; B later offers partial help (12) while C stays silent.

B-D.evidence: B tells D 'Go' and offers help (12); D first resists (16), then accepts the plan (18) and gives the handover, so they end up aligned.

C-D.evidence: C only declined to help (8); D never addressed C, and C said nothing after that. D did end up accepting that others take over.
